stage.description: What patterns are, how to describe them, and the principle of favouring composition over inheritance.

payload.markdown: This section provides an examination of patterns that help with storing and retrieving data and with mapping objects to and from databases.

blocks.text: This section provides an examination of patterns that help with storing and retrieving data and with mapping objects to and from databases.

items: Behavioral Patterns: Patterns that distribute responsibility and coordinate behaviour.
Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Creational Patterns: Patterns that control how objects come into being.
Data Mapper: A layer that moves objects to and from storage without the object knowing SQL.
Enterprise Patterns: Patterns for service layers, domain objects and application architecture.
Error Patterns: Repeatable strategies: fail fast, wrap and rethrow, aggregate and report.
Factory Pattern: Creating objects through a dedicated creator instead of new at every call site.
Object Identity: === compares instance identity: two objects with equal fields are still distinct.
